Together, these findings demonstrate that cocaine recruits a functionally specific NAc ensemble distinct from that recruited by shock, providing mechanistic insight into the valence-specific neuronal substrates underlying reward and aversion processing.

title: Aberrant single-subject cortical morphological networks and their associations with multiple symptoms in generalized anxiety disorder
abstract: Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) is a prevalent disorder associated with disrupted topological organization of large-scale brain networks. However, the morphological basis for network disruption and its clinical relevance remains unexplored. We constructed single-subject cortical morphological networks for 58 drug-free GAD patients and 86 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) separately based on cortical thickness, surface area, cortical volume, mean curvature, sulcal depth and local gyrification index. Between-group differences in local morphology and network topology were analyzed using general linear models. Partial correlation analyses were conducted to examine the relationship between brain alterations and clinical characteristics in GAD patients, while controlling for age, sex, education years and intracranial volume. Compared with HCs, GAD patients showed increased thickness in the left middle temporal gyrus and decreased local gyrification index in the left superior frontal gyrus. At the network level, GAD patients exhibited increased local efficiency, normalized clustering coefficient, and small-worldness, alongside decreased characteristic path length in cortical volume-based networks. Local morphology and network topological properties were associated with clinical characteristics such as illness duration, age of onset, anxiety severity, and personality traits. Our findings revealed both region-specific cortical abnormalities and global network reorganization in GAD patients. In particular, the shift toward stronger small-world configurations suggests enhanced local integration and global communication efficiency. These results highlight that GAD is associated not only with focal cortical alterations but also with systemic structural network changes that ma y underlie excessive anxiety and personality traits associated with the disorder.

title: Efficacy and safety of long-acting injectable aripiprazole in bipolar disorder: a multinational real-world target trial emulation
abstract: Long-acting injectable (LAI) aripiprazole is approved for maintenance treatment of bipolar disorder (BD), but real-world efficacy and safety evidence remains limited. Using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we conducted a target trial emulation among patients with BD who initiated oral aripiprazole between 2017 and 2023. Patients switching to LAI within one month were compared with those continuing oral therapy. After 1:1 propensity score matching on demographics, comorbidities, prior treatments, and laboratory data, hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for nine efficacy and safety outcomes were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models, with prespecified sensitivity and subgroup analyses. After matching, 1814 LAI and 1814 oral aripiprazole users were followed for a mean of 1.6 years. LAI use was associated with reduced all-cause hospitalization (HR 0.77, 95%CI 0.69–0.85) and emergency department visits (0.88, 0.79–0.98), with no difference in suicidal ideation or behavior (0.90, 0.75–1.08) or all-cause mortality (0.86, 0.55–1.37). Risks were higher for obesity (1.17, 1.06–1.29) and extrapyramidal symptoms (2.20, 1.38–3.50), but lower for major adverse cardiovascular events (0.73, 0.55–0.95) and hyperlipidemia (0.83, 0.72–0.97). Efficacy benefits were most pronounced in females and middle-aged or older adults; in adolescents, suicidal ideation or behavior was markedly reduced (0.49, 0.35–0.68). Sensitivity analyses showed similar trends. In BD, LAI aripiprazole was associated with better clinical outcomes without increased mortality compared with continued oral aripiprazole. The favorable benefit–risk profile supports broader consideration of LAI in maintenance care, with active monitoring of obesity and extrapyramidal symptoms.

title: Cyclopurine DNA lesions and repair in individuals with bipolar disorder and their unaffected siblings
abstract: Oxidative stress plays a key role in bipolar disorder (BD). 8,5’-cyclopurine-2’-deoxynucleosides (cPUs), including R- and S-cdA, are tandem oxidative lesions that distort the DNA helix, impair replication and transcription, and are primarily repaired by the nucleotide excision repair (NER) pathway. To date, cPU levels and NER gene expressions have not yet been studied in BD. This study assessed cPU levels and the expression of NER genes ( XPB, XPC, XPD, XPF, ERCC1 , and CSB ) in individuals with BD (n = 44), their unaffected siblings (n = 37), and healthy controls (HC; n = 46). Urinary cPU levels were quantified using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Expression of NER pathway genes were assessed in peripheral blood samples using quantitative reverse transcription PCR. cPU levels were significantly elevated in both BD and sibling groups compared to HCs, with R-cdA concentrations highest in siblings. NER gene expressions were also increased: XPB, XPF, ERCC1 , and CSB were upregulated in siblings, while XPC was elevated in both BD and sibling groups. XPB, XPF , and CSB levels were significantly higher in siblings than in the BD group, whereas XPD expression was increased in the BD group compared to both siblings and HCs. Elevated nucleotide damage and increased NER gene expression in individuals with BD and their unaffected siblings support prior evidence implicating oxidative DNA damage and repair mechanisms in BD pathogenesis. The identification of cPU lesions and distinct NER expression patterns highlights additional molecular markers and suggests a potential familial vulnerability contributing to the development of BD.

title: Exploring the effect of maternal autoimmune diseases on behavioral and social difficulties risk in children born preterm: evidence from EPIPAGE-2 study
abstract: Abstract Maternal immune activation (MIA) and preterm birth have both been associated with increased risk of autism spectrum disorder but their combined impact in preterm children is unclear. This prospective population-based cohort study used data from the French EPIPAGE-2 study, which included liveborn infants delivered at 22 to 34 weeks’ gestation in 2011 and followed them to 5 years of age. Neurodevelopmental outcomes at 2 years’ corrected age and at 5 years were assessed. Among 3609 children (155 [4.3%] exposed), maternal autoimmune diseases were initially associated with more impaired personal-social skills on the Ages & Stages Questionnaire at 2 years and a lower prevalence of high Social Communication Questionnaire scores at 5 years, but these associations were no longer statistically significant after adjustment. No significant associations were found between maternal autoimmune diseases and global developmental delay, ASD risk, or behavioral difficulties at 2 or 5 years in adjusted analyses. Subgroup analyses by gestational age and by exposure to immunosuppressive therapy also showed no increased risk. In this national preterm birth cohort, maternal autoimmune diseases during pregnancy were not associated with increased early behavioral or social communication difficulties in offspring. However, given the small number of exposed children, the predominance of endocrine autoimmune diseases, and the lack of immune activation biomarkers, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and warrant confirmation in larger, mechanistically informed studies

title: Altered GABAB receptor sensitivity in heavy drinkers indexed using a TMS-based biomarker: a randomized controlled experimental medicine trial
abstract: Abstract Metabotropic γ-aminobutyric acid type B receptors (GABA B Rs) are implicated in alcohol use disorder (AUD) and represent a promising therapeutic target. However, robust biomarkers of GABA B Rs target engagement and sensitivity in humans are lacking. We examined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)–derived cortical inhibition and growth hormone (GH) release as measures of GABA B R function, and whether heavy alcohol use is associated with altered responses to pharmacological GABA B R activation. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study, 31 healthy volunteers (16 heavy drinkers, 15 light drinkers) received baclofen 30 mg, baclofen 60 mg, or placebo across three sessions. Long-interval intracortical inhibition (LICI), short-interval intracortical inhibition, and intracortical facilitation were assessed with paired-pulse TMS at baseline and ~60 min post-dose. Baclofen blood concentrations and plasma GH levels were measured. Baclofen produced dose-dependent increases in GH release, confirming neuroendocrine GABA B R engagement. The LICI response to baclofen differed between groups: In light drinkers, baclofen at 30 mg potentiated LICI, and a similar potentiation was seen at 60 mg, indicating that a plateau may have been reached. In contrast, in heavy drinkers, a potentiation of LICI similar to that in light drinkers was seen at 30 mg baclofen, but was absent at the 60 mg dose despite comparable pharmacokinetics, suggesting altered GABA B R function. Effects were selective for GABA B R–mediated inhibition, with no consistent modulation of short-interval intracortical inhibition or corticospinal excitability. Acute baclofen administration reveals altered GABA B R sensitivity in heavy drinkers, with preserved responses at lower doses but reduced response under stronger agonist stimulation. LICI and GH release provide complementary biomarkers of central and peripheral GABA B Rs engagement and may support translational development of mechanism-based treatments for AUD.

title: Association between tirzepatide use and risk of suicidal ideation among individuals with obesity and major depressive disorder
abstract: Obesity and major depressive disorder (MDD) frequently co-occur and confer mutually reinforcing risks, including elevated suicidality. Tirzepatide has demonstrated substantial metabolic benefits, yet its psychiatric safety in high-risk populations with MDD remains uncertain. This study aimed to compare suicidal ideation outcomes among adults with comorbid obesity and MDD initiating tirzepatide versus non–GLP-1RA anti-obesity medications. This retrospective, propensity score–matched cohort study used deidentified electronic health record data from the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults (≥18 years) with diagnosed obesity and MDD who initiated tirzepatide or non–GLP-1RA anti-obesity medications were included. The primary outcome was suicidal ideation. Secondary outcomes included anxiety disorders, insomnia disorders, all-cause mortality, and emergency department or inpatient encounters. Among 24,103 matched pairs, tirzepatide use was associated with lower risk of suicidal ideation (HR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.42–0.93), anxiety disorders (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.81–0.86), insomnia disorders (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.86–0.98), all-cause mortality (HR, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.25–0.58), and emergency department visits or hospitalizations (HR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89–0.99). Risk reduction was generally consistent across prespecified subgroups. Control outcome analyses supported the internal validity of the findings. In conclusion, this study provides real-world evidence that tirzepatide initiation was associated with a lower recorded risk of suicidal ideation, as well as reduced anxiety, insomnia, all-cause mortality, emergency department visits, and hospitalizations, among adults with comorbid obesity and MDD. This observational association should not be interpreted as evidence of a direct antisuicidal effect. These findings support the potential for tirzepatide to serve as a metabolically favorable treatment option associated with a lower risk of suicidal ideation in this vulnerable, high-risk population.

title: Neurobehavioral changes in fear generalization in clinical high risk for psychosis
abstract: Changes in basic associative learning processes have been identified in several psychiatric conditions. However, it remains unknown whether these findings result from ongoing psychopathology or represent an underlying transdiagnostic risk factor for multiple clinical states. In this study, 72 participants with subclinical psychopathology, 23 of whom met criteria for the clinical high-risk for psychosis transdiagnostic risk syndrome (CHR+), completed a fear conditioning and generalization paradigm while functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data were collected. During this procedure, participants were presented with face stimuli that were either paired (CS+) or not paired (CS-) with a mild electrical shock, as well as eight face "morphs" (between the CS+ and CS-) tailored to each participant's perceptual discrimination ability. Following the scan session, participants rated the likelihood that each stimulus had been previously followed by a shock. Fear generalization-related neural responses and the memory ratings were then examined using both categorical and individual-level, psychometric modeling approaches. Expected patterns of fear generalization-related responses were observed in the anterior insula and superior frontal gyrus, and in the memory ratings. The psychometric modeling analysis revealed a significantly greater threshold in responses of the left anterior insula, representing a wider fear generalization curve, in the CHR+, compared to the control, group. Moreover, across the whole sample, symptoms of anxiety were associated with a wider fear generalization threshold. Thus, these findings suggest that specific features of one basic associative memory process, fear generalization, may be linked to CHR status and transdiagnostic risk for psychiatric illness.

title: Aerobic exercise prevents neuroinflammation and ameliorates depressive-like behaviors via suppression of HMGB1/NF-κB pathway-mediated reactive microglial states in mice exposed to chronic mild stress
abstract: Aerobic exercise is shown to have a positive effect on depressive-like symptoms; however, the associated mechanisms have not yet been fully elucidated. The role of neuroinflammation in the pathogenesis of depression is well-documented. High mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), a late mediator of inflammation, can promote the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines in various inflammation-related diseases. This study aimed to investigate the antidepressant effects of aerobic exercise by regulating hippocampal neuroinflammation via the HMGB1/NF-κB pathway-mediated microglial reactivity state. We assessed the depressive-like behaviors of the mice through behavioral tests. It was found that aerobic exercise significantly alleviated chronic mild stress (CMS)-induced depressive-like behaviors in mice. Furthermore, aerobic exercise reduced the total number of microglia and altered microglial morphology and reactive states in the hippocampus, accompanied by down-regulation of pro-inflammatory markers. These effects were observed to be regulated by HMGB1. We found a significant nuclear-to-cytoplasmic translocation of HMGB1 in the hippocampus, in the absence of apoptotic alterations (pyknotic nuclei, karyorrhexis, karyolysis), indicating an active release in the brain after CMS stimulation. Interestingly, aerobic exercise could reverse these alterations by inhibiting the HMGB1/NF-κB pathway. These findings not only enhance the understanding of the processes driving neuroinflammation in the hippocampi of mice exposed to CMS, but also highlight the potential of aerobic exercise as an anti-depression therapeutic strategy.

title: Exploring the relationship between oral microbiome and postoperative delirium in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma
TCF7L2 functionally relevant genetic variation with clinical implications in bipolar disorder with impaired glucose metabolism
abstract: Impaired glucose metabolism (IGM) and type 2 diabetes (T2DM) are common in bipolar disorder (BD). Genome-wide association studies have identified variation (rs7903146) in the gene encoding transcription factor 7-like 2 ( TCF7L2 ) as a well-established risk factor for T2DM in the general population and variation (rs12772424) showing a significant association with BD when accounting for BMI. Evaluating T2DM- and BD-associated TCF7L2 SNPs within bipolar IGM groups, along with their clinical correlates, could provide translational insights for future clinical practice. IGM was operationalized as evidence of prediabetes (fasting glucose of 100-125 mg/dL or glycated hemoglobin of 5.7%-6.4%) or T2DM. We compared sociodemographic, genetic, clinical characteristics, and course of illness measures between BD groups with and without IGM, then within BD subgroups (prediabetes, T2DM, and no IGM). Out of 850 BD patients included (mean age 49, SD = 13, 57% female, 8% non-White) 280 (33%) individuals had IGM. Compared to BD patients without IGM, those with IGM were older (p < 0.001), more likely to be non-White (p = 0.005), and obese (p < 0.001). The minor allele for the rs7903146 SNP (T2DM-associated SNP) was significantly greater in the IGM group compared to the group without IGM (11% vs. 5%, p = 0.009). There was no significant association between rs12772424 SNP (BD-associated SNP) with bipolar course of illness measures. Further investigation examining the complex interactions between functional genetic variants, molecular markers, environmental influence, and clinical phenotypes in BD is needed to better understand the mechanistic underpinnings to the high rate of T2DM bipolar comorbidity and identify early targets for treatment of both disorders.

title: Electroacupuncture alleviates chronic pain and comorbid depression through Gut-Metabolite-Brain axis remodeling to restore mPFC Glu/GABA balance
abstract: Abstract The comorbidity of chronic pain and depression is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder involving dysregulated microbiota–gut–brain communication. Although electroacupuncture (EA) has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for both pain and depression, the mechanisms linking peripheral microbial-metabolic remodeling to central neurotransmitter regulation remain incompletely understood. Here, we employed an integrated multi-omics approach in a spared nerve injury (SNI) rat model to investigate the gut–metabolite–brain mechanisms underlying EA’s efficacy. EA significantly alleviated mechanical hypersensitivity and depressive-like behaviors while restoring mPFC Glu/GABA balance, accompanied by normalization of the glutamate transporter EAAT2 and the GABA-synthesizing enzyme GAD67. Metagenomic analysis showed that EA remodeled the gut microbial ecosystem by increasing microbial diversity, suppressing opportunistic pathobionts, including Bacillus cereus, Alistipes onderdonkii , while enriching SCFA-associated genera, including Butyricimonas and Romboutsia . These alterations were accompanied by coordinated remodeling of amino acid and butanoate metabolism. Correlation network analysis identified Pipecolic acid as a central metabolic node linking gut microbial alterations with mPFC GABAergic neurotransmission and behavioral recovery. Although individual bacterial genera did not significantly mediate its restoration, causal mediation analysis demonstrated that the Pipecolic acid–GABA axis significantly mediated improvements in both mechanical allodynia and anhedonia, supporting Pipecolic acid as a functional metabolic hub linking peripheral metabolic remodeling to central GABAergic regulation. Collectively, these findings identify peripheral metabolic remodeling as a key mechanistic interface through which EA coordinates gut microbial ecology and central neurochemical homeostasis, providing a systems-level framework for understanding the therapeutic mechanisms of acupuncture in pain–depression comorbidity.

title: Large-scale EEG reveals shared and distinct neural oscillatory features across major psychiatric disorders
abstract: Major psychiatric disorders are leading contributors to global disability, yet robust biomarkers to inform diagnosis and treatment remain elusive. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a scalable, noninvasive approach to capture neural dysfunction, but prior findings have been inconsistent due to small, single-disorder cohorts. Here, we report a large-scale, two-site comparative study of resting-state EEG in schizophrenia (SCZ), bipolar disorder (BD), and major depressive disorder (MDD) compared with healthy controls (HC). Across 9751 participants’ EEG recordings, standardized preprocessing and feature generation yielded spectral power and functional connectivity (FC) measures tested with both statistical and machine-learning approaches. We identified convergent transdiagnostic alterations—reduced alpha power and increased gamma-band FC, implicating shared disruptions in inhibitory control and large-scale network coordination. Additional spectral differences included more pronounced delta-theta elevation in SCZ and a graded delta-theta continuum (SCZ > BD > MDD), suggesting a dimensional progression of neural dysregulation. Machine-learning models robustly distinguished individuals with psychiatric diagnoses from healthy controls within sites, but cross-site generalization and inter-disorder discrimination remained limited, underscoring challenges of heterogeneity. These findings identify reproducible EEG features that capture both shared and disorder-distinct neural alterations, advancing efforts towards early detection and individualized treatment in major psychiatric disorders.

title: Episodic memory-associated weighted atrophy network mapping in mild cognitive impairment and subjective cognitive decline: a multi-center study
abstract: This study localizes episodic memory-associated impaired networks in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and subjective cognitive decline (SCD) using a weighted key atrophy network mapping method, and investigates whether repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) can modulate them. Replicability was assessed across three independent cohorts involving 1312 subjects. First, single-subject key atrophy maps were constructed by comparing cortical thickness with cognitively normal groups and retaining regions showing significant thickness-memory correlations. Second, these maps served as seeds for functional connectivity analysis in a large normative connectome, generating atrophy networks weighted by atrophy extent. Third, group-level comparisons identified impaired networks in MCI and SCD, and methodological reliability was further validated against a memory network derived from patients with focal brain lesions. Finally, the impaired networks were experimentally modulated via a 4-week rTMS intervention (25 MCI, 13 SCD). Despite substantial individual-level heterogeneity, atrophied regions in most MCI patients were functionally connected to a common episodic memory-associated impaired network. This phenomenon was not significant in SCD patients. Both lesion-memory network mapping and cross-dataset validation confirmed consistency across cohorts. Critically, rTMS can modulate the impaired network in MCI patients, primarily reflected by enhanced functional connectivity within this network. In conclusion, this study developed a robust weighted key atrophy network mapping method, localizing common episodic memory-associated impaired networks in MCI/SCD. Modulation of this impaired network may serve as a potential therapeutic strategy to delay MCI progression.

title: Serum B-cell activating factor and delayed memory in first-episode drug-naïve schizophrenia: a case-control study
abstract: Cognitive impairment in schizophrenia has been linked to immune dysregulation, but the role of humoral immune regulators remains unclear. We examined serum B-cell activating factor (BAFF) and A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL) in 90 first-episode drug-naïve schizophrenia (FES) patients and 90 matched healthy controls (HCs). Cognitive performance was assessed using the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS), and symptom severity was assessed using the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS). Serum BAFF and APRIL were measured using Luminex technology. After adjustment for age, sex, education, BMI, and smoking status, serum BAFF and APRIL levels were significantly lower in FES patients than in HCs (BAFF: F = 131.935, P < 0.001; APRIL: F = 59.772, P < 0.001). In the hypothesis-driven primary analytic model focusing on RBANS delayed memory, the Group × BAFF interaction was significant ( F (1,171) = 13.524, P < 0.001), with a positive BAFF slope in HCs ( B = 0.015, P = 0.017) but a negative slope in FES patients ( B = -0.022). This interaction remained robust in sensitivity analyses. Exploratory analyses suggested a nominal Group × BAFF interaction for RBANS total score ( F = 5.866, P = 0.016, FDR-adjusted q = 0.082), which was interpreted cautiously. No analogous Group × APRIL interaction was observed, and BAFF/APRIL levels were not significantly associated with PANSS symptom dimensions. These cross-sectional findings identify peripheral BAFF as a hypothesis-generating correlate of delayed memory in early untreated schizophrenia, but do not establish temporality, causality, or central immune-cognitive mechanisms.

title: Integrative neuroimaging-transcriptomic analysis of neurodevelopment in adolescent-onset mental health problems
abstract: Abstract Mental health problems often emerge in childhood and adolescence, yet the neurodevelopmental and molecular processes underlying their onset remain poorly understood. Using longitudinal data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, we examined structural and functional brain cortical changes in youth who developed ADHD, conduct, anxiety, depressive, oppositional defiant, or somatic problems over a two year follow up period compared to healthy controls in five neuroimaging modalities (including structural MRI, resting-state fMRI, and task-based fMRI). We applied partial least squares (PLS) regression to link spatial patterns of neurodevelopmental changes to cortical gene expression profiles derived from the Allen Human Brain Atlas (AHBA). Pathway enrichment was assessed using spin-permutation-derived gene rankings. Significant neurodevelopmental alterations were observed in the ADHD and conduct groups only. PLS analysis further revealed significant spatial associations between their neurodevelopmental changes and gene expression distributions (Spearman rₛ >0.64). In ADHD, pathway enrichment highlighted mitochondrial respiration, oxidative phosphorylation, aerobic electron transport, ATP synthesis, and mitochondrial organization, with additional negative-end enrichment for synaptic protein interaction pathways. In conduct problems, all significant pathways were enriched among genes whose cortical expression patterns were inversely aligned with the conduct-problem imaging phenotype and involved translational machinery, ribosomal function, mitochondrial respiration, mitochondrial translation, protein targeting to mitochondria, and broader RNA/protein regulatory processes. These findings reveal distinct cortical transcriptomic patterns associated with adolescent-onset ADHD and conduct problems, with mitochondrial energy metabolism emerging as a prominent molecular correlate of ADHD-related cortical development and a distinct inverse transcriptional pattern characterizing conduct-related development. Together, our findings suggest that these externalizing problems are associated with neurodevelopmental alterations embedded within distinct cortical molecular contexts.

title: Non-suicidal self-injury in adolescents and young adults: an expert review
abstract: Abstract Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is highly prevalent among community and clinical adolescent populations and is associated with substantial psychiatric comorbidity, psychosocial impairment, and elevated suicide risk. This review synthesizes key findings on the development and maintenance of adolescent NSSI and discusses the clinical implications of this transdiagnostic behavioural phenomenon. It examines the prevalence and developmental course of NSSI, environmental and biological risk factors, proximal mechanisms, its conceptualization as an independent diagnosis versus a transdiagnostic risk marker, and current treatment approaches including their limitations. Current evidence indicates that adolescent NSSI emerges from interacting environmental risk factors (e.g. adversity and interpersonal stress) and neurobiological mechanisms related to emotional dysregulation, stress responsivity, and altered pain processing. While NSSI prospectively predicts suicidal behaviour, associations with other psychiatric disorders remain probabilistic and diagnostically non-specific. Overall, findings support conceptualizing NSSI as a transdiagnostic risk marker and behavioural phenotype linked to emotion dysregulation rather than as a distinct diagnostic entity. Adolescent NSSI reflects a dynamic biopsychosocial process involving emotional, neurobiological, and interpersonal mechanisms. Early detection and accessible intervention are essential to reduce chronicity, relapse, and the escalation of suicidal behaviour. Future research should prioritize mechanism-informed and personalized treatment approaches, improved identification of at-risk adolescents, and integration of developmental, neurobiological, and digital methodologies to advance prevention and intervention.

title: Temporal cortical gray matter volume relates to symptom improvement during cognitive behavioral therapy for depression
abstract: Abstract Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a first-line treatment for depression, yet treatment responses vary considerably. Understanding neurobiological factors associated with symptom improvement may help elucidate mechanisms underlying therapeutic change. This study investigated whether baseline cortical gray matter volume (GMV) is associated with reductions in depressive symptom severity during CBT. Therefore, n = 52 patients with unipolar affective disorders and at least mild depressive symptoms (according to BDI-II) and n = 42 healthy controls underwent clinical assessments and structural MRI at baseline; depressive symptom severity was reassessed after six months of outpatient CBT. Multiple regression analyses examined associations between pre-treatment cortical GMV and reductions in depressive symptoms under false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Additional models included anxiety, perceived stress, and childhood trauma as predictors. Compared to controls, patients exhibited significantly higher depressive symptom severity at baseline and greater symptom reduction over time (all p < 0.001). Within patients, baseline GMV of the right middle temporal gyrus (MTG) was significantly associated with symptom reduction (baseline–follow-up; β = 0.55, p FDR = 0.033). Right MTG volume accounted for additional variance in symptom reduction beyond established clinical variables (Δ R ² = 0.15). Group differences in GMV did not remain significant following FDR correction. These findings suggest that temporal gyrus GMV is associated with symptom improvement following CBT in unipolar depression, extending the focus beyond traditionally emphasized limbic regions. Preserved temporal morphology may support cognitive and emotional processes engaged during CBT, underscoring the relevance of temporal cortical structure for understanding the neurobiological correlates of psychotherapy response.

title: Temporal imprecision of the self in drug-free psychosis: Abnormal infraslow phase dynamics and brain complexity
abstract: Abstract Self-disturbance is a core feature of schizophrenia (SCZ) and may emerge during the prodromal phase. Temporal imprecision has recently been proposed as a core neural mechanism in schizophrenia, primarily demonstrated in faster EEG frequency ranges. Whether such imprecision extends to infraslow brain dynamics in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and relates to self-disturbance in early psychosis remains unknown. Here, we examined resting-state fMRI data from drug-free early psychosis patients (EP drug-free, n = 31, scanned before and after medication) and 31 healthy controls (HC). Brain dynamics were quantified using sample entropy (SampEn) and instantaneous peak frequency (PF) in regions associated with different layers of self-processing (interoceptive, exteroceptive, and mental). Compared to controls, EP drug-free showed higher SampEn and slower mean PF with greater variability than HC, particularly in the regions of the exteroceptive self. Moreover, EP drug-free exhibited a decoupling between SampEn and PF, whereas HC showed strong correlations. Both SampEn and PF significantly contributed to diagnostic classification, and increased SampEn was associated with greater severity of negative, disorganized, and anxiety/depression symptoms. Together, these findings indicate abnormal infraslow brain dynamics in early psychosis, characterized by increased neural complexity and disrupted temporal organization. This temporal imprecision, particularly within the exteroceptive self, may represent a key mechanism linking altered brain dynamics to self-disturbance and psychopathology in early psychosis.

title: Treating diagnostic frameworks as information systems: normative implications and opportunities
abstract: The DSM-5 and ICD-11 are not just clinical manuals; they are information architectures. Every time a clinician applies diagnostic criteria, every time a researcher aggregates symptoms into a diagnostic variable, and every time a committee drafts a revision, they operate on the same basic object: a coded system for transmitting information about mental states. Yet no one has applied information theory [ 1 ] to evaluate the architecture of diagnostic systems themselves. Existing applications of information-theoretic thinking in psychiatry — model-selection criteria such as AIC and BIC — assess how well statistical models fit covariance data; they say nothing about the efficiency of the diagnostic code itself. This Viewpoint argues that information theory (henceforth, IT) — the elsewhere highly influential mathematical framework developed by Shannon to characterize the capacity and efficiency of communication systems [ 1 ] — provides what is currently missing: a principled, quantitative basis for designing, evaluating, and reforming diagnostic frameworks and the instruments that operationalize them. The case for this reframing is not merely theoretical. Diagnostic quality, the product of validity and reliability in the DSM-5 and ICD-11 is, by available estimates, remarkably poor -essentially entailing that the majority of variability stems from measurement error or other irrelevant factors [ 2 , 3 ].

title: A precision health approach to medication management in neurodevelopmental conditions: a model development and validation study using four international cohorts
abstract: Abstract Psychotropic medications are commonly prescribed to children with neurodevelopmental conditions, but responses vary widely, prescribing is largely off-label, and the expertise required is concentrated in specialized programs. We developed artificial intelligence models to predict prescribing patterns of stimulants, anti-depressants, and anti-psychotics. Feasibility was established in research cohorts by predicting cross-sectional medication use from the Child Behaviour Checklist, with training and internal testing in the Province of Ontario Neurodevelopmental network ( N =598) and external testing in the Healthy Brain Network ( N =1,764) and Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development ( N =2,396) studies. Clinical evaluation used electronic medical records (EMRs) from the Psychopharmacology Program ( N =312) at Holland Bloorview Kids Rehabilitation Hospital to predict the medication class prescribed at a follow-up visit (∼3 months later). In all cohorts, the modelled outcome was the clinician’s prescribing decision, which reflects clinician judgement, family preference, tolerability, and access to care in addition to expected effectiveness, and does not directly measure treatment response or clinical benefit. In the research cohorts, internal testing achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (median [IQR]) of 0.75 [0.73,0.80] for stimulants, 0.83 [0.78,0.87] for anti-depressants, and 0.79 [0.72,0.86] for anti-psychotics, and external testing confirmed generalizability. In the EMR cohort, values were 0.84 [0.81,0.88] for stimulants, 0.82 [0.77,0.87] for anti-depressants, and 0.87 [0.83,0.91] for anti-psychotics. Findings demonstrate that AI can accurately learn expert prescribing patterns and predict medication prescribing decisions, supporting the potential of data-driven tools to guide personalized medication management for neurodevelopmental conditions.

title: Counteracting the overestimation of effect size in mass-univariate brain-wide association studies using cross-validation
abstract: Abstract Background Brain-wide association effects are commonly overestimated in psychiatric neuroimaging research, leading to low replicability and generalizability of findings, and ultimately to poor translation to clinical utility. Cross-validation is currently not standardly used in univariate neuroimaging analyses but could pose a potential counteracting measure for this problem. Methods We systematically evaluated the benefit of a cross-validation procedure to expose inflated effect size estimates in mass-univariate voxel-based analysis, using body mass index (BMI) as an example predictor for gray matter. A total of n = 3401 MRI scans from a psychiatric cohort were used to investigate the impact of applying cross-validation on effect size estimates across a range of sample sizes and across different localizations with a range of underlying pooled effect sizes. Results BMI was negatively associated with gray matter density with a maximum underlying effect size of R ² p = 0.036 (in the full sample of n = 3401). However, without cross-validation, effects were substantially overestimated in small samples, with effect sizes ranging up to R ² p = 0.535. Even with an underlying null-effect, effect size estimates up to R ² p = 0.429 were reached in samples with n = 25. Applying cross-validation revealed that these inflated effects in small samples did not generalize to novel data. A minimum sample size of n = 100 was required for largest brain-wide effects to start generalizing, while samples with n = 400 were needed for smaller effects to generalize. This ‘point of initial generalizability’ was not reached for underlying null effects, even with the maximum available sample of n = 3401. Conclusions Results suggest that cross-validation is an effective measure to expose overestimated effects in small samples and thus could help to counteract low replicability and generalizability in brain-wide mass-univariate association studies. Open-source code is provided for practical implementation.
